description: Dwyer et al. property specification patterns, LTL mappings, project surface syntax
source: Property Specification Patterns catalogue (SAnToS/KSU), LTL mappings page; transcribed into this project's parser syntax (G/F/X/U/W, ASCII, lowercase atoms p q r s t z). Known typos in the published ASCII (unbalanced parentheses) are resolved per the standard corrected reading and noted per entry.

patterns.intent: The event or state P never occurs at any point of the execution.
example_nl: the system never enters a deadlock state
no packet is ever dropped
the robot arm never crosses the safety boundary

patterns.intent: P never occurs before the first occurrence of R.
example_nl: no data is transmitted before the connection is established
before the oven is preheated, the tray is never inserted
the elevator doors never open before the cabin reaches a floor
patterns.notes: Standard before-scope convention: only executions in which r eventually occurs are constrained (the F r guard); vacuously true otherwise.

patterns.intent: After the first occurrence of Q, P never occurs again.
example_nl: after the account is closed, no withdrawals ever occur
once the emergency stop is pressed, the conveyor never moves again
after logout, no further commands are accepted

patterns.intent: P never occurs between any occurrence of Q and the next following occurrence of R.
example_nl: between takeoff and landing, the cabin doors never open
no configuration changes happen between the start and the end of an audit
between arming and disarming the alarm, the safe is never opened
patterns.notes: Only q-intervals that are actually closed by a later r are constrained (F r conjunct).

patterns.intent: After any occurrence of Q, P does not occur until R occurs; if R never occurs, P never occurs again.
example_nl: after a fault is detected, no new jobs are started until the fault is cleared
once the tank is sealed, no gas escapes until it is reopened
after the match starts, and until the referee whistles, no substitutions occur
patterns.notes: Weak until: unlike the between-scope variant, the interval need not close — if r never occurs after q, the prohibition on p extends forever.

patterns.intent: P occurs at least once during the execution.
example_nl: the process eventually terminates
a leader is eventually elected
the parcel is delivered at some point

patterns.intent: P occurs at least once before the first occurrence of R; if R never occurs, P is not required.
example_nl: a safety check occurs before the reactor reaches full power
before the session times out, the user logs in at least once
the backup runs at least once before the disk is replaced
patterns.notes: Weak until: vacuously satisfied when r never occurs; p is only forced on executions where r eventually happens.

patterns.intent: After the first occurrence of Q, P eventually occurs; vacuously true if Q never occurs.
example_nl: after the button is pressed, the light eventually turns on
once a job is submitted, it is eventually scheduled
after boot completes, the service eventually becomes ready
patterns.notes: Canonical site text has a stray trailing parenthesis ('[](!Q) | <>(Q & <>P))'); balanced here.

patterns.intent: Between any occurrence of Q and the next R, P occurs at least once; intervals that are never closed by R impose no obligation.
example_nl: between placing an order and receiving it, a payment occurs
in every trip between ignition and engine off, the seatbelt sensor triggers at least once
between check-in and check-out, housekeeping visits the room
patterns.notes: Weak until: if r never follows q, no p is required (open intervals are unconstrained).

patterns.intent: After any occurrence of Q, P eventually occurs and does so before the next R; P is required even if R never occurs.
example_nl: after the alarm sounds, the operator responds at least once before it is silenced
once a request is queued, it gets processed before the queue is flushed
after a fire is detected, and until the all-clear, the sprinklers activate at least once
patterns.notes: Strong until: this is the only difference from the between-scope variant — p is mandatory after q even when r never arrives.

patterns.intent: Transitions into the P-state occur at most two times over the whole execution.
example_nl: the system reboots at most twice
the airbag can deploy no more than two times
during its lifetime the battery is replaced at most twice
patterns.notes: The published catalogue fixes the bound at 'at most 2 designated states'; other bounds are obtained by unfolding the W-nesting further.

patterns.intent: Before the first occurrence of R, the P-state is entered at most two times.
example_nl: before the race ends, a driver may pit at most twice
at most two retries happen before the download completes
the pump activates at most twice before the tank is full
patterns.notes: Only constrains executions where r eventually occurs (F r guard).

patterns.intent: After the first occurrence of Q, the P-state is entered at most two times.
example_nl: after deployment, the service restarts no more than twice
once the exam begins, a student may leave the room at most twice
after entering degraded mode, the backup generator starts at most twice

patterns.intent: Between any occurrence of Q and the next R, the P-state is entered at most two times.
example_nl: between login and logout, at most two failed password attempts occur
between takeoff and landing, the autopilot disengages at most twice
at most two lane changes happen between entering and exiting the tunnel

patterns.intent: After any occurrence of Q, and until the next R (or forever if R never occurs), the P-state is entered at most two times.
example_nl: after maintenance mode starts, at most two test cycles run until normal operation resumes
once the breaker is energized, it trips at most twice until it is powered down
after boarding begins, and until the doors close, the gate agent reopens the gate at most twice
patterns.notes: Tail 'r | (!p W r) | (G p)' is verbatim from the catalogue: (!p W r) covers r never arriving after the second p-interval ends, and G p covers a final p-interval that never ends.

patterns.intent: P holds at every point of the execution.
example_nl: the pressure always stays below the threshold
the invariant holds at every step
the aircraft is always within its assigned corridor

patterns.intent: P holds continuously at every point before the first occurrence of R.
example_nl: before the gate opens, the warning light stays on continuously
the file remains locked at all times before the transfer completes
until liftoff, the umbilical cable stays connected
patterns.notes: Only executions where r eventually occurs are constrained (F r guard).

patterns.intent: After the first occurrence of Q, P holds at every subsequent point.
example_nl: after initialization, the watchdog is always enabled
once encryption is turned on, all traffic remains encrypted forever
after the contract is signed, the terms remain in force at all times

patterns.intent: P holds continuously between any occurrence of Q and the next following R.
example_nl: between ignition and shutdown, the oil pump is continuously running
the seatbelt sign stays on between takeoff and reaching cruising altitude
between check-in and check-out, the room is always marked occupied

patterns.intent: After any occurrence of Q, P holds continuously until R occurs; if R never occurs, P holds forever.
example_nl: after the door closes, it stays locked until the train comes to a stop
once the brake is applied, it remains engaged until the vehicle is stationary
after login, the session token stays valid until logout
patterns.notes: Weak until: the q-interval may never close, in which case p must hold forever.

patterns.intent: P does not occur until S has occurred first; if S never occurs, P never occurs (S precedes P).
example_nl: a resource is granted only if it was requested first
the missile can launch only after authorization has been given
no withdrawal happens unless a deposit occurred beforehand
patterns.notes: Weak until: satisfied by executions where neither p nor s ever occurs.

patterns.intent: Before the first occurrence of R, P can occur only if S occurred before it.
example_nl: before the deadline, a paper can be reviewed only if it was submitted first
before the system shuts down, data is written only after a checkpoint was taken
prior to the store opening, shelves are stocked only after the delivery arrives

patterns.intent: After the first occurrence of Q, P can occur only if S occurred first.
example_nl: after boot, the application runs only once the license check has passed
once the auction opens, an item is sold only after some bid was placed
after the shift starts, a machine operates only if a supervisor has signed off first

patterns.intent: Between any occurrence of Q and the next R, P can occur only if S occurred before it within the interval.
example_nl: between power-on and power-off, the motor spins only after the safety cover has been closed
between docking and undocking, unloading happens only after the ramp is secured
between the game start and the final whistle, points are scored only after the kickoff occurs

patterns.intent: After any occurrence of Q, and until R, P can occur only if S occurred first; the constraint also applies if R never occurs.
example_nl: after the alarm is armed, and until it is disarmed, the door opens only if a valid code was entered first
once a call starts, and until it ends, audio is transmitted only after the microphone is unmuted
after entering the tunnel, and until leaving it, the horn sounds only if a hazard was detected first
patterns.notes: Weak until: covers intervals that never close.

patterns.intent: Every occurrence of P is eventually followed by an occurrence of S (S responds to P).
example_nl: every request is eventually acknowledged
whenever the alarm sounds, the operator eventually responds
each submitted print job is eventually printed

patterns.intent: Before the first occurrence of R, every P is followed by an S that also occurs before R.
example_nl: before the trading day ends, every placed order is filled
before the system shuts down, every received message gets a reply
prior to the inspection ending, each fault that is raised gets repaired
patterns.notes: The response s must occur strictly before the scope-closing r (s & !r).

patterns.intent: After the first occurrence of Q, every P is eventually followed by an S.
example_nl: after initialization completes, every interrupt is eventually handled
once the service goes live, each query eventually receives a response
after the store opens, every customer who rings the bell is eventually attended

patterns.intent: Between any occurrence of Q and the next R, every P is followed by an S within the same interval, before R.
example_nl: between opening and closing time, every customer who takes a ticket is served before closing
between engine start and engine stop, every sensor fault triggers a warning before the engine stops
between connection setup and teardown, every ping receives a pong before the teardown
patterns.notes: The response s must land inside the interval (s & !r).

patterns.intent: After any occurrence of Q, and until R, every P is eventually followed by an S before R; the obligation also holds if R never occurs.
example_nl: after monitoring is enabled, and until it is disabled, every anomaly is eventually logged
once boarding begins, and until the doors close, every scanned boarding pass is confirmed
after the pump starts, and until it stops, every pressure spike is eventually vented
patterns.notes: Weak until: if r never occurs, the response obligation persists forever. Canonical site text is missing one closing parenthesis; balanced here (matches the seed corpus in tests/run_tests.py).

patterns.intent: P can occur only if it was preceded by an S and, after that S, by a T (the two-event chain S then T precedes P).
example_nl: access is granted only if a request was made and then approved beforehand
the rocket ignites only after the tanks were filled and then the launch area was cleared
a refund is issued only if a purchase occurred and a complaint was later filed

patterns.intent: Before the first occurrence of R, P can occur only if an S followed by a T occurred before it.
example_nl: before the product ships, it is packaged only if it was assembled and then inspected first
before the trial ends, a verdict is announced only after evidence was presented and then deliberated
prior to the launch window closing, ignition happens only if fueling completed and then the checklist was signed

patterns.intent: After the first occurrence of Q, P can occur only if an S followed by a T occurred first.
example_nl: after the plant starts up, the turbine engages only if the boiler was lit and then pressure was confirmed
once the course begins, a certificate is issued only if the student enrolled and then passed the exam
after the network comes up, a session opens only if a handshake happened and was then authenticated
patterns.notes: Canonical site text is unbalanced and reads '(!Q U (Q & <>P -> ...)'; resolved as q & ((F p) -> ...), matching the parenthesization the catalogue makes explicit in the 1-stimulus-2-response After-Q mapping.

patterns.intent: Between any occurrence of Q and the next R, P can occur only if an S followed by a T occurred before it within the interval.
example_nl: between shift start and shift end, a weld is made only after the parts were mounted and then aligned
between hospital admission and discharge, surgery happens only if the patient was examined and then anesthetized
between market open and close, a trade executes only after a quote arrived and was then validated

patterns.intent: After any occurrence of Q, and until R, P can occur only if an S followed by a T occurred before it.
example_nl: after the system is armed, and until it is disarmed, the gate opens only if a badge was scanned and then verified
once drilling starts, and until it stops, the drill descends only after the site was surveyed and then approved
after the oven turns on, and until it turns off, baking begins only if dough was loaded and then proofed

patterns.intent: A chain of S followed later by T can occur only if P occurred before the S (P precedes the chain S then T).
example_nl: a payment followed later by a shipment can only happen if an order was placed first
an alarm followed by an evacuation occurs only if smoke was detected beforehand
a download followed by an installation happens only after a license was purchased
patterns.notes: Canonical site text has a stray trailing parenthesis; balanced here.

patterns.intent: Before the first occurrence of R, a chain of S followed by T can occur only if P occurred before it.
example_nl: before the store closes, a fitting followed by a purchase happens only if the customer checked in first
before the flight departs, boarding followed by door closure occurs only if the aircraft was fueled first
prior to the merger completing, an offer followed by an acceptance occurs only if due diligence was done first

patterns.intent: After the first occurrence of Q, a chain of S followed by T can occur only if P occurred first.
example_nl: after the market opens, a quote followed by a trade occurs only if the account was funded first
once the lab opens, an experiment followed by a report happens only if the protocol was approved first
after the season starts, a semifinal followed by a final is played only if qualifications were held first
patterns.notes: Canonical site text is missing one closing parenthesis; balanced here.

patterns.intent: Between any occurrence of Q and the next R, a chain of S followed by T can occur only if P occurred before it within the interval.
example_nl: between dawn and dusk, a takeoff followed by a landing occurs only if a flight plan was filed first
between admission and discharge, medication followed by observation is given only if a doctor prescribed it first
between checkout and delivery, packing followed by dispatch happens only if the payment cleared first

patterns.intent: After any occurrence of Q, and until R, a chain of S followed by T can occur only if P occurred before it.
example_nl: after the plant is commissioned, and until it is decommissioned, a startup followed by full load occurs only if an inspection passed first
once the tournament starts, and until it ends, a semifinal followed by a final is played only if the group stage finished first
after the network is enabled, and until it is disabled, a login followed by a file transfer happens only if credentials were provisioned first
patterns.notes: Site text 'A U (R | P) | [](...)' resolved as '(A U (r | p)) | G(...)': the G-disjunct is the weak escape for when r and p never occur and no complete s-then-t chain ever starts.

patterns.intent: Whenever S occurs and is later followed by T, then after that T an occurrence of P eventually follows (P responds to the chain S then T).
example_nl: whenever a request is later followed by a timeout, a retry eventually occurs afterwards
if a temperature spike is later followed by a pressure spike, a shutdown eventually follows
whenever a bid is followed by a counterbid, the auctioneer eventually announces a decision

patterns.intent: Before the first occurrence of R, whenever S is followed by T within that region, P eventually follows the T.
example_nl: before the session ends, whenever a query is followed by an error, a diagnostic eventually runs afterwards
before the ship docks, whenever a warning is followed by a second warning, the captain is eventually notified
prior to the shift ending, whenever a jam is followed by a stoppage, a technician eventually intervenes
patterns.notes: In the canonical mapping the final 'F p' is not bounded by !r, so the response p itself may fall after the scope closes; published as-is.

patterns.intent: After the first occurrence of Q, whenever S is later followed by T, P eventually follows that T.
example_nl: after the reactor starts, whenever a coolant alarm is followed by a pressure alarm, an operator eventually intervenes
once the game begins, whenever a foul is followed by a second foul, a penalty is eventually awarded
after the pipeline is deployed, whenever a build failure is followed by a rollback, an incident report is eventually filed
patterns.notes: Canonical mapping uses X (!t U (t & F p)) — with !t rather than the F of the global variant — transcribed verbatim from the catalogue.

patterns.intent: Between any occurrence of Q and the next R, whenever S is followed by T within the interval, P eventually follows the T.
example_nl: between takeoff and landing, whenever turbulence is followed by an altitude drop, the crew eventually makes an announcement
between market open and close, whenever a dip is followed by a rebound, the analyst eventually files a report
between login and logout, whenever a failed write is followed by a retry, the cache is eventually flushed
patterns.notes: As in the Before-R variant, the final response p is not itself bounded by !r in the published mapping.

patterns.intent: After any occurrence of Q, and until R, whenever S is followed by T, P eventually follows the T.
example_nl: after monitoring starts, and until it stops, whenever a fault is followed by a second fault, a technician is eventually dispatched
once the line is energized, and until it is shut off, whenever a surge is followed by a flicker, the breaker eventually trips
after the watch begins, and until relief arrives, whenever a radar contact is followed by a confirmation, the bridge is eventually alerted
patterns.notes: The right-hand disjunct of the outer U (r | G(...)) is the weak escape covering the case where r never occurs.

patterns.intent: Every occurrence of P is eventually followed by an S and, after that S, by a T (the chain S then T responds to P).
example_nl: every order is eventually followed by a payment and then a shipment
whenever a fire is detected, an alarm eventually sounds and afterwards the doors unlock
each defect that is found is eventually triaged and then fixed

patterns.intent: Before the first occurrence of R, every P is followed by an S and then a T, all before R.
example_nl: before the office closes, every visitor request is followed by a badge being issued and then an escort arriving
before the release date, every reported bug is confirmed and then patched
prior to the voyage ending, every distress call is answered and then resolved
patterns.notes: The whole s-then-t chain must complete before the scope-closing r.

patterns.intent: After the first occurrence of Q, whenever P occurs, S holds at that very moment and T eventually follows.
example_nl: after the workflow is activated, whenever a form is submitted it is validated at once and later archived
once the plant is running, every alarm is acknowledged immediately and subsequently reported
after go-live, each transaction is instantly journaled and eventually reconciled
patterns.notes: The canonical After-Q mapping omits the eventuality before s: '[] (Q -> [] (P -> (S & o<> T)))', so s must hold at the moment p occurs. This is a frequently noted asymmetry in the published catalogue; kept verbatim.

patterns.intent: Between any occurrence of Q and the next R, every P is followed by an S and then a T within the interval.
example_nl: between login and logout, every file upload is followed by a virus scan and then an index update
between the race start and the finish, every pit request is followed by a pit stop and then a rejoin
between curtain up and curtain down, every cue is followed by a light change and then a scene shift

patterns.intent: After any occurrence of Q, and until R, every P is followed by an S and then a T.
example_nl: after the subscription starts, and until it is cancelled, every invoice is followed by a payment and then a receipt
once the furnace is lit, and until it is extinguished, every temperature alarm is followed by a damper adjustment and then a stabilization check
after the shift begins, and until it ends, every incoming call is followed by an answer and then a log entry
patterns.notes: The right-hand disjunct of the outer U is the weak escape for when r never occurs; note the escape's inner obligation 'p -> (s & X F t)' mirrors the immediate-s form of the After-Q mapping, verbatim from the catalogue.

patterns.pattern: Constrained Chain (1 stimulus - 2 response with constraint)
patterns.intent: Every occurrence of P is eventually followed by an S and then a T, and Z does not occur between the S and the T.
example_nl: every request is eventually granted and then completed, with no cancellation between the grant and the completion
each takeoff clearance is followed by a takeoff and then a climb report, with no abort in between
every payment is eventually authorized and then settled, with no chargeback between authorization and settlement
patterns.notes: The constraint z is forbidden only within the s-to-t window, not elsewhere.

patterns.pattern: Constrained Chain (1 stimulus - 2 response with constraint)
patterns.intent: Before the first occurrence of R, every P is followed by an S and then a T before R, with no Z between the S and the T.
example_nl: before the deadline, every draft is reviewed and then approved, with no rejection between review and approval
before the voyage ends, every distress call is answered and then resolved, with no escalation in between
prior to the store closing, every return is inspected and then refunded, with no dispute between inspection and refund

patterns.pattern: Constrained Chain (1 stimulus - 2 response with constraint)
patterns.intent: After the first occurrence of Q, whenever P occurs, S holds at that moment and T eventually follows, with no Z between the S and the T.
example_nl: after go-live, every ticket is immediately assigned and later closed, with no reopening between assignment and closure
once production starts, each batch is instantly sampled and then certified, with no contamination in between
after enrollment opens, every application is at once acknowledged and eventually decided, with no withdrawal between the two
patterns.notes: Like the unconstrained 1-2 response chain, the canonical After-Q mapping omits the eventuality before s (s must hold when p occurs); kept verbatim from the catalogue.

patterns.pattern: Constrained Chain (1 stimulus - 2 response with constraint)
patterns.intent: Between any occurrence of Q and the next R, every P is followed by an S and then a T within the interval, with no Z between the S and the T.
example_nl: between shift start and shift end, every order is picked and then packed, with no damage between picking and packing
between admission and discharge, every prescription is dispensed and then administered, with no substitution in between
between boarding and departure, every bag is scanned and then loaded, with no rerouting between scan and load

patterns.pattern: Constrained Chain (1 stimulus - 2 response with constraint)
patterns.intent: After any occurrence of Q, and until R, every P is followed by an S and then a T, with no Z between the S and the T.
example_nl: after the service is enabled, and until it is disabled, every alert is acknowledged and then archived, with no re-trigger between the acknowledgment and the archive
once the line starts, and until it halts, every jam is cleared and then logged, with no new jam between clearing and logging
after the watch begins, and until it ends, every contact is reported and then classified, with no loss of track in between
patterns.notes: The right-hand disjunct of the outer U is the weak escape for when r never occurs.

patterns.intent: If P occurs at least once, then S must also occur somewhere in the execution (before or after P); unordered co-occurrence.
example_nl: if a payment is made, a receipt must also be issued at some point
whenever an error is logged, an alert is also raised somewhere in the run
if the file is opened, it must also be closed at some point in the trace
patterns.notes: DECLARE process-mining template (Pesic & van der Aalst), NOT part of the Dwyer property-specification catalogue. Unordered co-occurrence; Global scope only. Source: IBM nl2ltl declare.py RespondedExistence.to_ltlf.

patterns.intent: P and S are mutually exclusive: they cannot both occur in the same execution.
example_nl: a transaction is never both committed and rolled back
the door is never both locked and open during a run
manual mode and automatic mode are never both activated in the same session
patterns.notes: DECLARE process-mining template (Pesic & van der Aalst), NOT in the Dwyer catalogue. Mutual exclusion; symmetric (F p -> !F s is equivalent to F s -> !F p, BLACK-verified). Global scope only. Source: IBM nl2ltl declare.py NotCoExistence.to_ltlf.
